# Maximum drawdown (`max_drawdown`)

*Category: Drawdowns · Nature: observed · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `max_drawdown@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Largest peak-to-trough decline of compounded wealth.

## 2. Formula

```text
min_t( W_t / max_{s<=t} W_s - 1 ), W_0 = 1, W_t = prod_{i<=t}(1 + r_i)
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

The worst loss an investor would have suffered buying at a high point and selling at the following low point.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Path-dependent realized loss; always shown. Expected maximum drawdown grows with history length and volatility (Magdon-Ismail & Atiya, 2004), so compare only across similar horizons.

## 7. Assumptions

- Wealth index starts at 1 before the first return.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Short histories: drawdown statistics grow with the length of the track record and cannot reveal risks that have not yet materialized.
- Returns are smoothed, which reduces measured drawdowns.
- Data frequency is low: intra-period declines are invisible.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

One observation; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `path_risk`: Path statistics (drawdowns, streaks) are computable from one observation but are unrepresentative below 3 years (low) and 5 years (moderate); longer histories tend to reveal deeper drawdowns.)

## 11. Sources

- Magdon-Ismail, M., & Atiya, A. (2004). Maximum Drawdown. Risk, 17(10), 99-102.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Signed (negative = loss); the inception value counts as a peak so a first-period loss is a drawdown (decision 0007).
